html:
The Turkish invasion of Cyprus began on 20 July 1974 with landings near Kyrenia, five days after a coup backed by the military junta in Athens overthrew President Makarios.

Turkey said it was acting as a guarantor of the 1960 settlement to protect the Turkish Cypriots. In a second offensive in August, after talks failed, its army took about 37 percent of the island. Around 160,000 Greek Cypriots fled or were driven south, and some 45,000 Turkish Cypriots moved north. Thousands died, and many remain missing. The junta in Athens fell. In 1983 the north declared itself the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, recognised only by Turkey. The island has stayed divided, and the Annan Plan failed to reunite it.
sum: The Turkish invasion of Cyprus began on 20 July 1974 with landings near Kyrenia, five days after a coup backed by the military junta in Athens overthrew President Makarios.
